segments.title: Chương 41: 0041【Hãy tự tin nói ra hoài bão của bạn】
segments.content:
17577 Forum.

The site admin, Can Ying, was chatting with several partners on QQ.

They had already created multiple versions of "17577 Legend," mainly earning money by running a private server platform, building server frameworks, and developing tools.

"Holy crap, Abyss Legend is maxed out with 5,000 players."

"We've been running private server platforms for so long, and this is the first time we've seen someone proactively cut off the download link."

"Yeah, in the past, we were always worried about having too few players. This time, they're actually afraid of having too many players and crashing the server."

"Just got back from reading the post. I'm gonna die laughing."

"Laugh your ass off. They're making a fortune, alright?"

"Who's gone in and played it?"

"I got to level 19, but it was so laggy I quit."

"I'm doing quests right now. I heard you can get an Abyss Map teleport scroll as a reward."

"What's that?"

"It's like an entry ticket to a hidden map. The monsters in the hidden map are insane, and the equipment they drop is insane too. They make money by selling these tickets. Of course, players don't have to spend money either. You can get one ticket by doing quests, and there's a chance it'll drop from mutated monsters."

"This gameplay is pretty fresh. We could copy it."

"What's so fresh about it? It's just imitating a foreign game. The Abyss Map is basically a dungeon."

"Who cares who they're imitating? As long as it makes money, that's what matters. Let's make one too!"

"We'll talk about it another day. I'm gonna go run the Abyss Map."

"How about we develop a cheat for unlimited tickets?"

"That's fucking dirty. Can you not be so disgusting? We have to have some standards, even when running private servers."

"What the hell are you talking about? You've made and sold private server cheats for money before!"

7GG Forum.

This gaming forum was on the verge of overtaking its competitors to become the largest private server hub in the country.

It had too many experts, earning it the reputation of being the Whampoa Military Academy of the private server world!

Dudu Legend was one of their products.

"Bro, have you played Abyss Legend?"

"I was just about to pay to run the Abyss Map in the Woma Temple when you called. It's not so laggy now."

"I'm in the game too. Just topped up. Let's do the Abyss together! By the way, I'm using my old ID."

"Hurry over, I'll send you the coordinates."

"This Abyss dungeon gameplay has a lot of potential. Should our private server imitate it too?"

"Sigh, let's sort out our internal conflicts first. The more money we make, the more ideas the brothers have. We argue every day. Sooner or later, we're gonna fall apart!"

"..."

The internal strife among the experts at 7GG Forum had become extremely serious.

Everyone thought they were hot stuff, but felt they weren't getting paid enough.

At this very moment, one expert, after playing Abyss Legend, had already decided to imitate the dungeon gameplay and go solo.

It was estimated that in another week or two, a slew of private servers featuring dungeon gameplay would follow suit.

After 10 p.m., the server became slightly smoother, and players' levels had also risen, leading to a growing number of people topping up their accounts.

The number of top-ups would likely be even higher tomorrow, as a large number of players needed to wait until daytime to make bank transfers, or go through the trouble of remittance at the post office.

Those who chose post office remittance often didn't even have a bank account!

In this era, UnionPay was still in its promotional phase. It was perfectly normal for players not to have a bank account.

Four people were responsible for communicating with players who were topping up. They would send the player IDs to Yang Yuhui, and then Yang Yuhui would issue the tickets to the players. The one confirming the payments and tallying the total amount was Chen Guiliang's cousin, Feng Tao.

Feng Tao had a day job, so he would definitely need to be replaced.

Arranging for him to tally the top-up amounts today was, naturally, Tao Chenggang's way of reassuring Chen Guiliang.

As for players at internet cafes, they topped up with the cafe managers. The managers sent the game IDs over, and Yang Yuhui would then issue the tickets to the players. Once the total top-up amount reached a certain level, the managers would deduct their commission and transfer the money into the bank account supervised by Feng Tao.

Tao Chenggang walked around and said, "The work of collecting money and issuing tickets is relatively easy today. It'll probably get a bit busy tomorrow. We'll see then if we need to add more people."

"Whatever Brother Gang arranges is fine. We have full confidence," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

"You little punk... never mind, let's talk about something else."

Tao Chenggang asked, "Should we accept an interview with Popular Software magazine?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Of course. Since we've already made it big, we might as well make it even bigger and put a little media pressure on Shanda."

Yang Yuhui said, "We also need to keep an eye out for cheats. Once we find one, we ban the account!"

"I'll arrange for people to handle that," Tao Chenggang said.

It wasn't just official games that had a headache with cheats; private servers did too.

The active period for private server cheats hadn't arrived yet. After the special crackdown next New Year's Day, some private server platforms would be scared into shutting down directly, while others would lay low. At that time, everyone's income would plummet, and some experts would start frantically selling cheats.

Only after the storm had passed and private server platforms became active again would the big shots and experts of the private server world join forces to suppress the cheats.

"There's a player topping up called Lao Du, who wants to chat with Zui Wo Hong Chen and Yi Jian Xi Lai!" shouted one of the underlings responsible for liaising with players.

Zui Wo Hong Chen and Yi Jian Xi Lai were the two founders of the Abyss private server that Chen Guiliang had made up.

Chen Guiliang said in pleasant surprise, "We've run into an expert."

This Lao Du would still be famous twenty years later. Who in the Legend private server, web game, and mobile game industries didn't know him?

This person later developed the "Little Torch Engine," which could easily create and mod Legend at will.

Chen Guiliang had Lao Du add his QQ: "Hello, I'm Zui Wo Hong Chen."

"Haha, I've heard so much about you. Your Abyss gameplay is very interesting. I couldn't resist topping up to run the Abyss," Lao Du complimented him on QQ.

They chatted casually after that; it was just an initial contact.

Lao Du was also an expert from the 7GG Forum. Things were very unpleasant on his end, and he was thinking about leaving 7GG to go solo.

He was very skilled technically, but not so much in operations.

Therefore, he was reaching out to the Abyss Legend team, thinking perhaps they could cooperate and complement each other in the future.

"Guiliang, come over, the interview is starting!"

Old Wei, an editor from Popular Software: "Hello, are you Zui Wo Hong Chen or Yi Jian Xi Lai?"

"Yi Jian Xi Lai," Tao Chenggang replied.

"It's a pleasure to meet you. I play games often myself. I work at Popular Software, mainly writing articles related to online games."

"I've long admired your work. I've loved reading your magazine since I was a child."

"Haha, now that you put it that way, I feel old."

"Not at all, not at all. You are a senior in the field."

"Can you tell us about your real-life experiences?"

Tao Chenggang turned to Chen Guiliang and asked, "How should I spin this?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Ninety percent truth, ten percent fiction."

Tao Chenggang immediately typed his reply, "My parents were both employees of a state-owned enterprise, and I joined one too after graduating from a junior college. But as a young person, I couldn't stand the monotony, so I quit my job and went to a coastal city to try my luck. I changed jobs many times, even working as a security guard for a hotel and a manager at an internet cafe. In the summer of '98, I joined UTStarcom, promoting the PHS 'Xiaolingtong' service in the Yangtze River Delta."

"You were an employee of UTStarcom!" Old Wei was instantly excited. Including this in his report would make it a much better story.

Tao Chenggang typed, "A former employee. After the Xiaolingtong market stabilized in the big cities, I was sent to promote it in third and fourth-tier cities. It was then I discovered that IC telephone cards were still in a very early stage of promotion in these cities. So I resigned from UTStarcom and started selling IC cards as an agent."

"You must have made a lot of money, right?"

"I made a few hundred thousand in two years. Later, the market became saturated, the profit margin for IC cards was very low, and the competition was fierce, so I returned to my hometown to open an internet cafe. It was because of the internet cafe that I became addicted to The Legend of Mir."

Old Wei felt it was getting more and more sensational, "Your life experience is particularly exciting. It's clear you're a go-getter."

"Haha, you flatter me."

"How did you come up with the idea of making a private Legend server?"

"It's just as I said in the post. Zui Wo Hong Chen is a friend I made in the game. He took a train to come have a drink with me. We talked about a lot of people and a lot of things. We were both drunk at the time, and on an impulse, he went to the forum and posted."

"Didn't you ever think of making money from the private server?"

"I'm not short on that kind of money. I have eight internet cafes and a computer store. I'm too busy with my legitimate businesses to bother with a gray area industry like private servers."

"You think private servers are a gray industry?"

"After the Abyss private server blew up, I specifically consulted a lawyer. The relevant laws are still a blank slate, but it does violate copyright law. Private servers aren't black or white; they can only be considered a gray industry."

"Do you want legislation for private servers?"

"Ah. I'm just an ordinary person with no power or influence. Naturally, I hope the laws of our country will become more comprehensive."

"But that would affect your private server's earnings."

"I don't rely on the private server for money. If I can't do it, I'll just stop."

"But based on the current situation, the Abyss private server can make a huge profit."

"That was an accident."

"If Shanda demands you shut down the private server, would you agree?"

"It depends on the situation. The Abyss private server no longer belongs to just me; it's a sanctuary for many gamers. If Shanda wants me to shut down the game, they have to come up with a solution. The players are already refugees from Legend. Are they supposed to become refugees again?"

"Why do you think the Abyss private server became so popular?"

"The players' resentment towards Shanda is too great. Many of them came over out of spite."

"Isn't it because the Abyss Map gameplay mentioned in the post is very interesting? How did you guys come up with this idea?"

"All the ideas came from netizens. The power of the masses is limitless; they have all sorts of weird and wonderful ideas. All the changes in Abyss Legend came from suggestions by enthusiastic netizens. I just spent the money to help them realize it."

Seeing this, Chen Guiliang gave Tao Chenggang a thumbs-up.

Tao Chenggang chuckled.

"Do you also have a lot of resentment towards Shanda?" Old Wei asked again.

Chen Guiliang said, "My turn."

Tao Chenggang immediately stood up from the computer.

Chen Guiliang typed, "I used to, but not anymore."

"Why?" Old Wei asked.

"I was afraid of going to jail, so I consulted a lawyer and looked up a lot of news about Legend. The reason Legend couldn't be updated for over half a year was, at its core, because the Korean side was too greedy. The Korean company actually wanted to obtain Shanda's user database. This is a game company's core secret. If I were Mr. Chen, I wouldn't agree either."

"So, you believe the fault lies with the Korean side?"

"Of course it's the Korean side's fault. A game development company demanding an operator's user database, they think they're God Almighty. Mr. Chen already gave them a lot of face by sending a copy of the database as per the contract. Although there were problems with the database, the contract wasn't clear about it in the first place. They could have just let it go, but the Korean side unilaterally terminated the cooperation. In this matter, it's 100% the Korean side that breached the contract first."

"It seems you're on Shanda's side."

"I'm not on any company's side. I only stand for morality and law."

"What are your plans for the future?"

"Making games is quite fun. I might develop and operate my own games in the future. Haha, I definitely don't have enough startup capital. I hope some big boss will invest."

"The current Chinese online game market is almost completely dominated by foreign games. Chinese game companies tend to act as agents for foreign products. Are you confident that you can develop your own game and succeed?"

"Isn't there still Westward Journey Online?"

"The four games Legend, Mu, CrossGate, and Westward Journey Online 2 account for 50% of the market share this year. Among them, only Westward Journey Online 2 is domestically produced. If you count the next few games, the market share of Japanese and Korean games is over 85%."

"I have always believed that Chinese people are no worse than foreigners; we just started later. Within ten years, domestic games will be able to reclaim 75% of the market share!"

"You firmly believe that domestic games can be revitalized?"

"Yes. The internet has spawned a huge market, and online gaming is part of it. There's still negative press about it being a 'spiritual opium,' but one day, the gaming industry will become a part of China's economic prosperity. We can't just stand by and watch foreign manufacturers take all the money!"

"How do you think the game industry should be developed?"

"Legislation needs to be improved; that's at the national level. For practitioners, at this stage, we should absorb and imitate foreign game technology and concepts. The next step is to innovate while imitating."

"Like making cars?"

"You could say that. But both the auto and game industries have a fatal problem. The big companies act as agents for foreign products and can make money lying down. Some even make money on their knees. Why would they take risks and stand up straight to earn money?"

"How can we break through?"

"This requires someone to blaze a trail. I am willing to be a pioneer in the Chinese game industry, to pave the way through hardship! Even if I lose everything, I can still serve as a lesson in trial and error for those who come after."

"I'm feeling a little fired up listening to this. I wish you success."

"Thank you."

After chatting for a while longer, Old Wei asked, "Can I interview Zui Wo Hong Chen as well?"

"He's a student and doesn't want to be disturbed."

"Still a student?"

"Yes. I can give you his QQ, but I doubt he'll say much."

"..."

The interview ended.

Tao Chenggang scrolled through the chat log, "Are you extending an olive branch to Shanda?"

Chen Guiliang smiled, "And helping you promote your game at the same time. Maybe we can attract a few investors."

Just then, an underling shouted, "Boss Tao, someone wants to top up 3000, and he says his surname is Shi..."

Shi Yuzhu, Chairman of Giant Group. Representative product: "This holiday season, don't accept any gifts; if you must, accept Nao Bai Jin."

A veteran Legend player, game ID: Only_Accept_Nao_Bai_Jin. Because he couldn't become overpowered even with pay-to-win, he was banned multiple times for using one-hit-kill cheats and quit the game in a rage.

He later independently developed ZT Online, the first domestically produced online game with unlimited pay-to-win.
